mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -45.6% to -36.7% over four weeks, indicating a sustained recovery trend. This momentum continues linearly over the next four weeks, producing further gains in retail-and-recreation mobility.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 8.9 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or reverses by more than 5 percentage points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stabilized near -33% in the most recent week after declining from -43.4%. When transit stabilizes above -35%, commuter confidence returns within two weeks, driving retail footfall recovery as workers resume shopping patterns near workplaces and transit hubs.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -35% and remains stable for one week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -43.4% to -33.0% over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls below -35% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not show positive week-on-week change within 14 days of TRANSIT stabilization.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC are coupled through shared essential-shopping behavior. GROCERY_PHARM recovery from -21.7% to -11.3% signals normalized household provisioning routines. This behavioral normalization extends to discretionary retail within one week, accelerating RETAIL_REC gains.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -12% in any week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week of GROCERY_PHARM crossing -12%, or the correlation between weekly changes in GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC becomes negative.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered to near-baseline (0.7%) while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated (8.7%), indicating outdoor activity substitution for indoor retail. If PARKS continues to rise above 5%, outdoor recreation crowds out retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 5% in any week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points over the next 28 days despite PARKS rising above 5%, or RESIDENTIAL falls below 5% while PARKS remains elevated.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility remains severely depressed at -44.3%, indicating continued remote-work policy or voluntary avoidance. If WORKPLACES does not recover above -40% within two weeks, retail-and-recreation mobility will remain suppressed because office-adjacent shopping and commute-time retail visits remain unavailable.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -40% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -30% over the next 14 days while WORKPLACES remains below -40%, or WORKPLACES recovers above -35% within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL elevation (8.7%) combined with RETAIL_REC depression (-36.7%) indicates a regime where home-based activity dominates. Over four weeks, if RESIDENTIAL remains above 8%, the home-preference regime persists, capping retail recovery at -30% or worse.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 8% for all four weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL elevated at 8.7% in most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves by more than 5 percentage points over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above 8%, or RESIDENTIAL falls below 7% within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are jointly suppressed (-33.0% and -44.3%), indicating coordinated avoidance of public spaces. Recovery requires both to rise simultaneously. If TRANSIT rises above -30% AND WORKPLACES rises above -40% within one week, retail confidence returns sharply within the following week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -30% AND WORKPLACES rises above -40% in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:Both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show recent improvement
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 2 percentage points within one week of both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES crossing their thresholds, or only one series crosses its threshold.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has recovered faster than RETAIL_REC (10.4 vs. 8.9 percentage points), indicating essential-shopping normalization precedes discretionary retail. If GROCERY_PHARM reaches -8% or better within one week, discretionary retail follows within two weeks as consumer confidence spreads.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises to -8% or better in any single week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 3 percentage points within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM reaching -8%, or GROCERY_PHARM reverses below -12% before RETAIL_REC responds.
